guenh...@mindspring.com wrote:
>
> To All,
> I know that the VTES-L server was hit by a power surge or some such,
> but does anyone know if the list is active again, or what needs to be
> done to make it so? Any other info would be appreciated...

It is active again, but the subscriber list was not restored (problem
with the backups, I guess).

Anyway, if you aren't getting the messages, you'll have to resubscribe
by sending mail to

list...@oracle.wizards.com

with the command

SUBSCRIBE VTES-L <firstname lastname>

in the body of the message (without the angle brackets, of course).

If you don't want digest mode (you want each message to be mailed to
you as it is received by the list), include the command

SET VTES-L NODIG

after the SUBSCRIBE command.

P.S.
I sent e-mail to everyone who was subscribed in July of last year who
is no longer on the list to re-subscribe -

did anyone get this message, or did it fall into the bitbucket as well?

--

>> I know that the VTES-L server was hit by a power surge or some such,
>>but does anyone know if the list is active again, or what needs to be
>>done to make it so? Any other info would be appreciated...

>What's on the list that's not on this newsgroup? Why not just keep
>all discussion here? Or are the topics somehow different?

Several reasons come to mind... when Ryan Dancey (of FRPG fame) was
actually talking to us, he only used the VTES-L as his means of
communication. It's a good way to stay in touch with WotC contacts,
and receive announcements from them (many businesses deny their
employees newsgroup access during the day, for obvious reasons. This
prevents it as an easy means for their communication). And it saves
the muck of downloading all of the rules questions that are posted for
LSJ to the newsgroup (he bounces all replies to the VTES-L).
Oh yeah, V:EKN uses it fairly often, too...
